plain_text:
1 
 
Meeting Minutes 
 
 
Salem Bicycling & Shared Path Advisory Committee 
 
Wednesday, August 5, 2026 | 6:15 p.m. 
 
City Hall Annex 1st Floor Meeting Room & Via Remote Participation 
 
Members Present: John Wathne (Chair), Josiah Guthrie (Vice Chair), Annie Wolf, 
Emmylou Manwill, Matt Caruso, Craig Bilodeau, Alexa Ogno 
Members Absent:  Kevin Jordan, Josh Nagle 
Also Present:  Tom Devine, Senior Planner 
 
Call Meeting to Order 
 
Wathne calls the meeting to order. 
 
Public Comment 
 
Wathe opens the meeting to public comment and there is none. 
 
Discussion of Bike Master Plan 
 
Guthrie leads a discussion about the future direction of the committee, asking who the 
group wants to connect with and what it wants to be known for. Members discuss 
opportunities to build momentum and visibility for cycling in the community through 
expanded social media outreach, partnerships with organizations such as the Police 
Department and Parks & Recreation, participation in events like Notch rides, and 
initiatives such as valet bike parking and group rides. The committee also considers 
whether it should be known for reviewing plans and revisits the mission statement on its 
webpage as part of a broader conversation about goals and priorities. 
 
The group discusses the possibility of raising funds and whether donations should be 
managed through the City or a nonprofit organization. Members note that any 
expansion of activities requires sufficient volunteer capacity and support. Several 
resources and potential partners are identified, including Kylie Sullivan, who can provide 
insight into the Main Streets volunteer model. Wolf has experience with nonprofit 
management. Manwill notes that the committee has allies who may be able to support 
future efforts. Councilor Holappa shares examples from Beverly's slow rides program 
and discusses strategic planning processes used by businesses, as well as the 
evolution of Mack Park Food Park from a city initiative into a nonprofit organization. 
 
Discussion of forming a nonprofit is tabled until the next meeting. Guthrie agrees to 
gather additional information based on his experience with the Scholarship Committee. 
The committee agrees to continue discussing organizational goals, partnerships, and
2 
 
nonprofit options at future meetings. Caruso agrees to invite Kylie Sullivan to attend a 
future meeting, and Devine will look into how the city works with and supports 
associated non-profits. 
 
Discussion of Proposed Committee Logo 
 
The group tables this item to the next meeting. 
 
Complete Streets Prioritization Plan Follow Up 
 
The group confirms their comment letter is the final version and notes that their 
comments have been incorporated into the City’s online map created for the plan. 
 
Bike Share Program Updates 
 
Devine reports that he will be reaching out to neighboring communities to discuss 
expansion. The group discusses the lack of a Bluebikes station at the train station. 
Devine reports that the City is seeking approval from the MBTA. The group suggests 
communicating to the MBTA that there is urgency to get it in place before October. 
 
Events 
 
Devine shares information about several upcoming events, including Volt & Vibe, which 
is scheduled for Saturday, September 19, from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. along the Salem 
State University bike path. This requires advance registration. He also highlights the 
SERC potluck, which takes place on Wednesday, August 26, at 6:30 p.m. at the Willows 
and requires an RSVP. In addition, Devine notes the upcoming Proctor Street Walk 
Audit, scheduled for Tuesday, August 25, at 4:30 p.m., with participants meeting at 
Gallows Hill Park. 
 
Bike Theft in Salem 
 
Manwill expresses interest in improving bicycle security. Councilor Holappa suggests 
exploring the Project 529 bicycle registration program and notes that information has 
been shared with the Police Chief. The committee discusses gaps in existing bike 
parking guidelines, particularly regarding security, and observes that many bicycles are 
not locked properly. Members consider a public education campaign on proper bike 
locking techniques and discuss the need to ensure bike racks are securely anchored. 
The university is identified as a potential partner in supporting bicycle security initiatives. 
The group suggests adding an option to See-Click-Fix to request a bike rack, the same 
way there is the option to request a tree planting. 
 
Potential DPW Attendance at Future Meeting 
 
The group discusses how to approach a conversation with the DPW Director if he is to 
attend a future meeting. Devine remarks that the DPW Director is a dedicated public
3 
 
servant who deserves respect. The group wishes to continue discussing the matter at 
the next meeting. 
 
Transportation Commission Update 
 
Ogno states that the Transportation Commission did not meet last month. 
 
Staff Update 
 
Devine reports that the Governor’s bill based on the Micromobility Commission’s 
recommendations passed the state Senate and now needs approval by the House of 
Representatives. It appears that this bill includes all of the recommendations that are 
within the legislature’s authority to enact. 
 
Devine announces that Connor Ryan resigned from the Committee, resulting now in a 
total of two vacancies. 
 
The group wishes to continue meeting at 6:15pm. 
 
Devine reflects on the recent death of Boston Transportation Planner Louisa Gag. 
 
Meeting Minutes 
 
No draft minutes are available for review. 
 
Adjourn 
 
Bilodeau motions, Guthrie seconds, and all vote in favor to adjourn at 7:54pm. 
 
*** 
 
Approved by the Bicycling & Shared Path Advisory Committee on 10/7/2026.
